platform: Scorpion (agency CMS) — footer credit and form host confirm it
purpose: OPERATOR REFERENCE ONLY. Not design DNA. The owl template is the sole source of layout and structure.
strengths: Genuinely deep, well-written service copy — roofing, commercial, and remediation pages each carry real substance, not filler.
Real trust assets already in hand: Florida CGC licence number published, BBB A+, Top 20 Home Depot contractor, award badges, three named reviews.
Named leadership team with headshots — seven people, roles listed.
Own project photography for both commercial and residential work, plus before/after sets.
weaknesses: The brand is invisible. The claw mark — the one thing that makes this identity memorable — appears once, at roughly 40px, in the header logo and nowhere else on 8,235px of page.

Chrome is navy/slate, not the brand's black-and-crimson. The claw red shows up only as small button fills and inline link colour, so the page reads as a generic agency template with a red accent rather than as Wolfpack.

Hero is centered light-weight all-caps text over a photo of the company's own building and van — low contrast, no CTA hierarchy beyond a single small button, and it sells 'design-build excellence' rather than a reason to call.

The people are buried. 'Meet The Pack' is a third-level nav item; the homepage never shows a face, despite the fact that named-humans is this business's strongest differentiator against ghosting competitors.
No visible process, no timeline, no 'here is what happens after you call' — which is precisely the anxiety Orlando homeowners report.
Reviews render as a plain unstyled quote list with no rating, no source, no count. 4.9 across 63 Google reviews is never stated.
Very long single-column scroll with repeated identical value-prop blocks (the same five 'Why Wolfpack' bullets appear verbatim on home, about, and residential pages).
Heavy cookie-consent and third-party widget load (reCAPTCHA, Roomvo assistant, Scorpion analytics) on every page.
opportunities_for_rebuild: Make the four-streak claw the structural signature of the site — section dividers, hero rake, hover states, numbered process steps — not a logo detail.
Go black and crimson. Kill the navy. The identity is already high-contrast and aggressive; the site should match it.
Put the pack on the homepage. Faces, names, roles, above the fold or immediately below it.
State 4.9 / 63 Google reviews and the CGC licence number in the hero trust row.
Replace the repeated bullet blocks with one named process ('The Wolfpack Way') and one guarantee ('One Quality. One Price.').
